headline: Gravity isn't a force pulling you down—it's space curved by mass
universal_truth: What seems like force is often the shape of the system we're in
fun_facts: Einstein showed gravity isn't a force—it's the curvature of space and time caused by mass
You're falling toward Earth right now; the ground is pushing up to stop you
GPS satellites must account for gravity's effect on time or they'd be wrong by miles
discussion_questions: What other 'forces' in your life might actually be shaped by your environment?
How does knowing gravity is curved space change how you see falling?
What would daily life be like in zero gravity?

hook.script: Newton said gravity is a force that pulls objects together. Then Einstein came along and said: there is no force. Objects just follow straight paths through curved space. The apple doesn't fall—the Earth curves up to meet it. That's not poetry. That's physics.

cliff.script: If gravity isn't really a force, why does it feel like one? Why do we feel heavy? Einstein's answer revolutionized physics—but what did he actually discover about gravity that Newton missed?
cliff.prompt: What is gravity according to Einstein?

options.text: Mass curves the fabric of space-time, and objects follow that curve
options.response: Yes. Imagine a bowling ball on a trampoline—other objects roll toward it not because of force, but because of the curved surface.

options.text: A force field that radiates from massive objects
options.response: That's Newton's view—Einstein saw something deeper...

fact1.title: Curved Space-Time
fact1.script: Imagine placing a bowling ball on a stretched rubber sheet. The sheet curves around it. A marble rolled nearby follows that curve toward the bowling ball. That's gravity—not a force, but geometry. Mass tells space how to curve; space tells mass how to move.

fact2.title: You're Always Falling
fact2.script: Right now, you're in free fall toward Earth's center. You don't feel it because the ground pushes up against you. That 'push' is what you experience as weight. Astronauts feel weightless not because there's no gravity—but because they're falling freely with their spacecraft.

fact3.title: Gravity Slows Time
fact3.script: Gravity warps not just space, but time. GPS satellites experience time slightly faster than we do on Earth's surface. Without corrections for this time dilation, GPS would be off by miles. Einstein's theory isn't just elegant—it's essential for modern navigation.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What feels like external force might be the shape of the system you're in. Before blaming the pull, examine the curvature. Sometimes the environment, not the force, determines the path.

outro.script: That's Day 33. Tomorrow, we'll explore how magnets work—another invisible force that shapes our world. Until then, feel your weight—and know it's just the Earth's curved space-time pressing against you.

growTrack.title: Gravity Awareness - Feel the Fall
growTrack.activity: Drop something small and watch it fall. Now imagine: it's not being pulled down—it's following a curved path through space-time, and the ground is rushing up to meet it. How does this reframe change the experience?
